input.brief: Ahmed Wagdy, DevOps / Platform / MLOps engineer in Cairo; runs AI gateways, GPU clusters, Kubernetes, CI security gates

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Name band and rails
hero.blueprint: One viewport filled completely with tiles on 8px gaps and 8px margins. Across the top, a band tile 170px tall holds the name on one line at clamp(140px, 14.4vw, 220px), heavy, tracking -0.04em, centred and deliberately wider than the band so both ends are cropped by the tile's edges (overflow: hidden, white-space: nowrap). Under it a row of four equal tiles, 64px tall, each holding one text link at 16px, top-left aligned. The remaining 62% of the height is three columns. Left rail (columns 1-2): two stacked tiles, a portrait photograph above and a short list of five facts below. Centre (columns 3-10): one large photograph tile, object-fit: cover, with a statement tile in the ground tone laid along its bottom third holding one sentence at clamp(24px, 2.4vw, 36px), top-left aligned on 24px padding. Right rail (columns 11-12): a full-height stack of five flat colour tiles, a light-to-dark run from the palette; the lowest takes the accent colour and holds the single action, the others each carry one short fact at 15px.
hero.mobile: Tiles restack in two columns with 6px gaps. The name band stays full width: 26vw type cropped at both sides in a 110px band. The four link tiles become a two-by-two block. The large photograph tile follows at full width, 4:3, with the statement tile under it at 6vw. The colour rail becomes a horizontal row of five short tiles, the action tile last and twice as wide.
hero.headline: The name on one cropped line, any length, plus one sentence of up to 60 characters in the statement tile.

type.name: Bricolage Grotesque

display.settings: weight 600 · tracking -0.04em · leading 0.92 · sentence case; leave optical sizing on so large sizes tighten and gain contrast

type.note: A grotesk with visible stroke contrast and slightly irregular curves, so headings look drawn rather than engineered. Suits reports, consultancies and design-led software that want warmth without a serif.

palette.name: Graphite and orange
palette.note: Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate, graphite taking about two thirds, and photographs are desaturated so nothing competes. Safety orange marks the buttons, one thick solid bar across the top of the page and the highlighted item in a list or chart.

motion.name: Edge-to-edge marquee
motion.description: One line of very large type travels sideways across the full width at a slow constant speed, as a band between two sections or as the closing statement. Linear timing, duplicated content for a seamless loop, paused on hover and under reduced motion. One marquee per page, carrying real words (the name, the claim), never a list of buzzwords.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: Names as one paragraph
sections.blueprint: All project or client names run together as one paragraph at poster scale: 10–18 names at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 78px), leading 1.1, flowing inline across the full width between 24px margins and wrapping where they fall, five to seven lines in all. Names are separated by a comma, or by a small inline frame: an `inline-block` 0.8em tall and 1.2em wide, aligned to the cap height, holding that project's photograph and placed directly after its name. Every name is a link; all names rest in the soft ink, and the hovered one takes full ink while its inline frame scales to 1.6 times from its left edge. A heading of two words opens the paragraph as its first words in full ink, on the same line and at the same size, followed by a colon. Below the paragraph at the left margin, one line at 15px gives the count and the years covered.
sections.mobile: The paragraph is set at 9vw, left-aligned, about twelve lines, with names separated by commas. Inline frames are removed except after the first three names, where they stay at cap height. All names are full ink; each remains a link with 6px of extra line spacing for touch.

sections.name: Statement, table pushed right
sections.blueprint: A heading of four to six words spans the full width on two lines at clamp(40px, 4.5vw, 68px), left-aligned with its first line indented 3vw and leading 0.98. 96px below, the table is pushed into the right-hand five columns (8–12) and the left stays open. One plain word naming the table (offices, hours, rates) hangs at 14px in column 7, top-aligned with the first row. Each row is a three-part line at 15–16px with 26px between rows: the kind or day in the soft ink at the left of the measure, the place or service at 30%, and the address, time or price right-aligned, with a small arrow where the row links. Rows are separated by space only; every fourth row has 44px above it to form groups. In columns 1–4, bottom-aligned with the last row, one 4:5 photograph 22vw wide may sit alone. Holds 5–14 rows.
sections.mobile: Heading at 9.5vw without the indent. The table takes the full width at 16px; each row stacks the kind above the place, with the value right-aligned on the first line. The naming word is dropped because the heading already says it. The photograph follows at 60% width on the right margin.

sections.name: Quotation spread edge to edge
sections.blueprint: A full-width field with no image. One short quotation, six to ten words, is set at about 9vw in the display face and broken by hand into two or three lines. Each line is a flex row with `justify-content: space-between`, so its first word sits hard against the left margin, its last word hard against the right, and any middle word floats between them. Lines are 0.6em apart, far looser than a headline, which lets the gaps read as pauses. The attribution is spaced the same way on a final row at 18px: name at the left margin, role centred, organisation at the right. Opening and closing quotation marks belong to the first and last words. There is no separate heading. Leave at least 140px of empty field above and below, and give the field its own flat colour when the palette allows.
sections.mobile: Lines break after every two words and keep the spread: one word at each margin, at 13vw. A single-word line alternates between the left and right margins. The attribution stacks as three short lines at 15px, aligned left, centre and right in turn.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: The email as display type
sections.blueprint: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
sections.mobile: The address breaks after the @ onto two lines at 11.5vw, left-aligned, sitting at 55% of an 86svh screen. The sentence sits at the top-left at 18px. Phone, city and social links stack at the bottom-left at 15px with 12px between them.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: Produx Design
references.idea: The wordmark is the hero, and the showreel image assembles itself from scattered square fragments as you scroll.
references.hero: Near-black field with 80px side margins. The wordmark, in a wide, light-weight uppercase sans with a slashed O, runs margin to margin (about 89% of the width) with a cap height near 20% of the viewport, starting 9% from the top. A large empty gap follows. In the lower half a two-line statement at 5.1vw sits flush left; opposite it, bottom-aligned to the statement and flush to the right margin, is a three-line paragraph in small monospace about a quarter of the width. No nav bar, button or image in the first viewport; the bottom quarter is empty.
references.type: At Aero in light-to-medium weight for the wordmark, the 74px statement and project titles; DM Mono for the hero paragraph, bracketed nav items and uppercase project blurbs at about 11px. Three sizes; the statement is roughly five times the mono text.
references.colour: #0e0e0e #e4e4e4 #545e54 #303930 #6f8f3a — Near-black page with off-white type and no accent colour. Colour arrives only through imagery: moss green and sage in the showreel render, then each case-study thumbnail brings its own palette.
references.imagery: A 3D render of a moss-covered boulder on a sage background, first broken into scattered square tiles, then whole as a 16:9 inset. Work thumbnails are square-cornered stills and video in mixed ratios, including one vivid orange-violet gradient card.
references.layout: 80px margins. After the hero, a small logo top-left and four bracketed mono links spread across the right half. Hero is all type, the next three screens are a pinned image assembly, then a work grid with unequal column widths and mono captions under each thumbnail.

sections.description: Pinned showreel reveal on black. Eight to ten small square tiles, 60 to 100px, each a different crop of the same image, float scattered around the centre at different depths, some blurred. As scroll advances they multiply, enlarge and lock together until they form one 16:9 image inset at about 70% of viewport width, with the wordmark centred on it in white and tiny captions overlaid at left and lower right.

Two unequal columns on black, roughly 52% and 30% of the width with a wide gutter. Each item is a square-cornered thumbnail with a row of small rectangular mono tags along its bottom edge; beneath it a small square bullet, the project name in the sans at about 16px and a two-line uppercase mono blurb. The next item breaks the grid: a single thumbnail centred at about 75% width.

steal: Run the wordmark margin to margin in a light weight rather than a heavy one; thin strokes at huge size read as assured instead of loud.
Pair one large sans statement with a tiny monospace paragraph bottom-aligned on the opposite margin and leave the middle of the row empty.
Introduce the hero image as scattered square crops of itself that converge into the full frame on scroll.
references.media: The fold has no media at all; the first picture is the 40s showreel, which arrives on the second screen as scattered square tiles at different depths that converge into an inset 16:9 frame, then fills 56-96% of each screen until it is full-bleed at about 4850px. Below: a staggered two-column mosaic with a centred wide interlude, a logo strip bleeding off both edges, and a pinned 3D stone centre-right with the statement docked bottom-left; zero radius everywhere.
references.motion: Black at 400ms, then wordmark letters rise one by one out of a baseline mask, tagline words rise in masked lines and the small blurb types itself out, settled by about 2.2s. Lenis drives a sticky, scrubbed hero in which tiles fly in from depth, blurred to sharp, assemble the frame and scale it to full bleed, then headings resolve through a pixel-slice glitch, work frames reveal by inset clip, the manifesto colours word by word and the closing stone grows moss as the ground turns from black to moss green, all as per-frame script (44,246 style mutations) with no GSAP exposed.

references.name: Kereliott
references.idea: A quiet house gets a quiet page: one dark field, one typeface, the name set as wide as the screen and photographs left to drift in generous darkness.
references.hero: Very dark green-black field with cream type. A two-line introductory sentence at about 30px sits top-left inside 30px margins; a small cream rectangular button sits top-right. The upper half is otherwise empty. The house name fills the full content width in a flared humanist sans, mixed case, with capitals about 19vw tall, its baseline at roughly 87% of the viewport height. Immediately beneath, separated by a gap of a few pixels, the top sliver of a full-width landscape photograph enters from the bottom edge.
references.type: A single face, Trust, in regular weight: a humanist sans with flared terminals and old-style figures. The wordmark is an oversized graphic; all other text is one size of about 20-30px plus tiny 10px photo captions. Hierarchy is position, not weight.
references.colour: #161c1a #eae8dc #222926 #1f2926 — Cream on green-black from top to bottom with no accent colour. The map is drawn in a tone barely lighter than the ground, so photographs supply all the colour.
references.imagery: Natural-light photos of a stone cottage, garden and deck with square corners, in mixed portrait and landscape crops at differing sizes. One full-width opener, then small images placed singly with tiny captions under the left corner.
references.layout: 30px margins, text held to the left 60% in one size. Photographs are staggered left and right at different widths with large dark gaps between, like pictures passed on a wall. The name and a booking button stay fixed in the top corners.

sections.description: A full-width landscape photograph runs margin to margin directly under the wordmark, followed after a gap by a four-line paragraph in the single text size, left-aligned and spanning about 85% of the width. There is no heading or label; the text simply continues the sentence begun at the top of the page.

After a left-aligned paragraph, a silhouette map of the region sits centre-left, about half the viewport wide, filled in a green only a few percent lighter than the background. Five towns are marked with small ring dots and tiny labels; only the house's town has a solid cream dot. No border, legend or frame.

Photographs are placed one or two per screen in a stagger: a portrait image about 30% wide against the left margin, a larger near-square one starting lower against the right margin, later a landscape image top-right of centre and a smaller one bottom-left. Each has a 10px caption under its left corner. More than half of every screen is empty dark ground.

Two short left-aligned sentences in the standard text size with underlined inline links to booking platforms and an email address, then a small cream certification badge. The footer is a single line at the very bottom: social link left, copyright centre, three underlined utility links right, with a tall empty gap above.

steal: Size the wordmark to fill the content width exactly and let the first photograph tuck directly under its baseline.
Draw a location map as a tone-on-tone silhouette with one filled dot among ring dots.
Use a single typeface in one weight and essentially one text size, creating hierarchy through placement and emptiness.

references.name: Julien Calot
references.idea: Each series of paintings is a full-screen close crop of one canvas, with the series title, year and piece count strung along a single line at mid-height like a museum wall label.
references.hero: A painting detail fills the viewport edge to edge, a face in the centre with saturated landscape shapes around it and the canvas weave visible. All text is white and small, with no scrim. Top-left: the artist's name in bold condensed capitals about 45px tall, the largest type on screen. The same top row holds a two-item filter at 29% across and two small stacked link groups at 75% and 95%. On the vertical midline a single row reads: year at the far left, series title in condensed black caps at 1.6vw about 10% in, and a piece count preceded by a short dash at the far right. No button.
references.type: FF DIN Pro Condensed Black in uppercase with +0.02em tracking for the wordmark and series titles (23px); Doner, a wide bold sans, for tiny uppercase nav and meta at about 9-10px. Only two text sizes besides the wordmark; type is kept deliberately small against the art.
references.colour: #c76802 #2f7fc9 #2e7d3a #7a4fa0 #fafafa #bdbdbd — The interface has no colour of its own: white type over whichever painting is on screen, so each panel takes the painting's oranges, blues, greens or violets. The single-series view switches to flat light grey.
references.imagery: Photographed paintings in a saturated naive style, used two ways: enormous full-bleed crops showing brushwork and weave, and small complete canvases with linen edges and soft drop shadows in a horizontal row on grey.
references.layout: A stack of full-viewport panels, one per series, identical in structure: fixed header along the top, one label row at mid-height, nothing else. Margins are about 20px. Opening a series swaps the crop for a grey wall with one row of evenly spaced small canvases.

sections.description: Six or more consecutive full-screen panels, each a different painting cropped far tighter than its frame so a detail fills the screen. The same three-part label row sits at exactly 50% height on every panel: date range at the left edge, series title in condensed caps starting about 10% in, count of pieces at the right edge. The fixed header overlays all of them unchanged, so scrolling reads like turning plates in a book.

Flat light-grey viewport. A single horizontal row of small portrait canvases, each about 11% of the viewport wide and 24% tall, photographed with their fabric edges and a soft shadow, spaced roughly 5% apart and vertically centred; the row runs off both sides. The series label row overlaps the first canvas. About 70% of the screen is empty grey.

steal: Crop artwork far past its edges to fill the screen and keep all text under 2vw, so the image does the shouting and the type behaves like a wall label.
Run a panel's metadata along one horizontal line at mid-height: date at the far left, title a tenth in, count at the far right, repeated identically on every panel.
Contrast full-bleed immersion with a sparse detail view: tiny complete works in a single row on flat grey with 70% of the screen left empty.
